edition.alertText: Israel election deadlocked — exit polls show no majority for Netanyahu or Eisenkot blocs; Brent falls to $113.88 (-1.67%) as Tehran diplomacy eases fears; Houthis claim Ras Tanura refinery strike (550k b/d); CNN: US can strike Iran within 96 hours; PGSA warns Sinokor vessels face 'legal action' from Nov 1; Iran Navy says dark tanker hit mines and caught fire; Saudi intercepts 3 ballistic missiles and 7 drones from Houthis

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 242 with the conflict's trajectory now hanging on two pivots — a deadlocked Israeli election and a Moscow diplomatic summit that produced atmospherics but no breakthrough. Exit polls from Israel's October 27 vote showed neither Netanyahu's right-wing bloc (50–60 seats across four networks) nor Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar!-led opposition (43–53 seats) reaching the 61-seat Knesset majority, with weeks of coalition-building ahead and official results due November 4. Turnout hit 55.7% in the first nine hours — the fastest pace on record — underscoring public frustration with the war. In the strait itself, Iran's armed forces chief reiterated that it is 'completely closed' to uncoordinated traffic, and the Iranian Navy reported that a dark (AIS-off) oil tanker hit mines and caught fire in the eastern strait. The PGSA issued a new warning that Sinokor Merchant Marine vessels would face 'legal action' starting November 1, with at least seven ships already subject to 'appropriate actions.' The PGSA non-compliant blacklist stands at 123+ vessels. October has set a wartime record with at least 28 attacks on commercial vessels in and around the strait (Washington Institute for Near East Policy), more than double the monthly average. IMO has recorded 120 incidents since the war began, with more than 30 VLCCs damaged — about 3.5% of the global fleet. CENTCOM rejected IRGC claims of US withdrawal from the strait as 'false,' saying US and partner forces remain deployed.

Oil markets continued their retreat on Tuesday as Saudi-Iran-Turkey-Pakistan diplomacy offered a faint prospect of dialogue. Brent crude settled at $113.88 per barrel, down $1.93 (-1.67%), while WTI fell $1.86 to $99.90 (-1.83%) — marking WTI's first close below $100 since late September. The pullback from last week's $117+ Brent peak reflected Qatari-mediated talks and Iran signaling flexibility on a 4–5 day strait reopening period, though no concrete terms emerged. UBS now expects Brent to hold near $110 through year-end, up from its earlier $100 forecast. Gold slipped below $4,000 per ounce to around $3,995, pressured by US-China trade optimism that eased safe-haven demand, after breaching $4,100 earlier in the month. VLCC tanker rates held near record levels at $1.2–1.4 million per day for Gulf-to-East Asia routes, with freight adding $33–41 per barrel to delivered crude — more than a quarter of the price. Newcastle coal remained near $150 per tonne, up 40% year-to-date. The Brent prompt spread widened to approximately $5 from $3.69 the prior week, signaling tightening physical markets despite headline price relief.

The Houthi-Saudi front escalated further as Yemen's militia widened its target set to include Saudi energy infrastructure. The Houthis claimed a missile strike on Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery, which processes approximately 550,000 barrels per day — the claim was reported by Reuters but remains unconfirmed by Saudi authorities. Saudi air defenses intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province, four drones targeting southern regions, and three more drones over Riyadh, with debris from the Riyadh intercepts damaging a building and vehicle but causing no casualties. The Houthis denounced Egypt's parliamentary authorization of military support for Saudi Arabia as a 'declaration of war,' raising the specter of a broader regional conflagration. In Moscow, Putin hosted both Iran's President Pezeshkian and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit, where Pezeshkian told Putin the region can resolve its problems without the US. Qatar's office confirmed the leaders discussed the war, negotiations, the Strait of Hormuz, and energy supplies — though Iranian state media's readout made no mention of the war. Iran's security chief Rezaei subsequently met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, urging Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan to sever security ties with Washington. CNN reported that US forces maintain the capability to launch major strikes on Iran within 96 hours of a Trump order, targeting energy, military, and nuclear sites — though no decision has been made, with midterm elections on November 3.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne feeding into phosphate production costs — Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic idling South Fort Meade phosphate plant (Florida) for 6+ months from Dec 8 due to sulfur shortage. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain near zero since early September (WTO Hormuz Trade Tracker). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). UNCTAD's de la Mora warned at Doha forum (Oct 25) that farmers cutting fertilizer will hit 2027 crops; African nations face critical fuel/fertilizer shortfalls. Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG exports still crippled — QatarEnergy signed historic deal to buy 4M tonnes/yr US LNG from Cheniere through 2054. Putin hosted Qatar's Emir at GECF summit Oct 27 to discuss energy supplies. Dutch TTF gas near €90/MWh. Japan's trade deficit doubled to ¥2.82T ($17.8B) on higher energy costs. Kpler: Asian LNG prices to rise amid simmering geopolitical tensions.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
